title: How to align elements in Canva on Mac: step by step with Position and Tidy up
metaTitle: How to Align Elements in Canva on Mac (Step by Step)
description: Learn how to align elements in Canva on Mac: select two or more objects, open Position in the top toolbar, and pick an edge or center.
targetKeyword: how to align elements in canva on mac
intro: To align elements in Canva on Mac, select two or more elements by holding Shift and clicking each one. Then click Position in the top toolbar and choose Left, Center, Right, Top, Middle or Bottom.
tldr: Select two or more elements with Shift-click, then open Position in the top toolbar.
Pick Left, Center, Right, Top, Middle or Bottom to line the selection up.
Use Space evenly for three or more elements, and run Tidy up after you align.
The only Mac shortcut confirmed in these sources is ⌘G for grouping.
Lazur can circle the Position button and guide each click. It does not click for you.

blocks.text: What you need before you start

You need the Canva desktop app for Mac and a design with at least two elements on the page. Alignment only works on elements you can select. Everything in this guide is written for the desktop app. Canva's own Help Center pages returned errors when this page was checked, so the steps come from third-party tutorials. Where those tutorials disagree, this page says so.

blocks.title: Not verified by Canva
blocks.text: No official Canva page was read for this guide. Test the steps on a copy of your design before you use them on a client file.
Pick the right edge or center

Position holds six align options. Left, Center and Right line elements up horizontally. Top, Middle and Bottom line them up vertically. Choose the option that matches the job. If product cards should share a top line, pick Top. Middle would center them up and down, which gives a different result.

blocks.text: For a multi-element selection, the tutorials describe Canva lining up against the combined outline of everything you selected. That detail comes from a tutorial, not an official page. Read the result before you move on, and use Undo if it looks wrong.
Align one element to the page

One element is a grey area. One tutorial says the align options don't appear with a single element selected. A search snippet says a single element aligns to the design page. Neither claim is confirmed. Select two or more elements to be safe, and test the single-element case on a scratch design if you need it.
Space evenly for three or more elements

Space evenly is the option people miss. It applies when three or more elements are selected. It sets equal gaps between the elements, horizontally or vertically. Use it for a row of icons, a set of name cards, or a column of buttons on a flyer.

Space evenly is not in every tutorial. One guide lists it under Position. Another tutorial covering the same align tools does not mention it at all. Open Position on your own version and look before you plan a layout around it.
Worked example: a row of product cards

Say you have a social post with a row of product cards. Some cards sit a little higher than others, and the gaps look random. Select all the cards with Shift-click. Choose Position > Top to put them on one top line. Then open Position again and choose Space evenly to set equal gaps.
Align first, then space. If you space cards that sit at different heights, the gaps look even but the tops still wobble. Line up the tops, then fix the gaps.
Second example: a flyer header and a logo

Flyers often mix a big headline, a logo and a column of details. Select the headline and the logo, then choose Center so they share a middle line. Next, select the detail lines and choose Left so every line starts on the same edge. Two alignments and two selections give you a clean page.
Snap guides, rulers and grid

While you drag an element, red lines appear when it lines up with another element or the center of the page. Release the element when the lines show. That is the fastest way to line things up by eye, and it needs no menu.

For a steadier check, turn on rulers and grid from the View menu. Choose View > Show rulers and View > Show grid. One cheat sheet mentions R for the ruler, but it lists Windows keys and gives no Mac equivalent, so use the menu.

blocks.title: Snap guides vanish after you drop
blocks.text: Snap guides only show while you drag. After you drop an element, use the rulers and grid to check where its edges sit.
Tidy up and the uneven gaps problem

Tidy up adjusts spacing so a group of elements looks more even. It helps when a set is almost right but not quite. The tutorials give one order for it: align first, then run Tidy up. Tidy up gives odd results when the elements are still misaligned.

Think of Tidy up as the last pass. Use it after the edges and centers match. If the result still looks wrong, undo, align again, and run Tidy up once more. Running it on a messy layout only makes the mess harder to read.
Groups and text boxes trip people up

Grouping and aligning are different jobs. Grouping decides what moves together. Aligning decides where things sit. If a headline, a caption and an icon should move as one block, group them with ⌘G first, then align the group. Otherwise each piece moves on its own.

Text boxes cause the most confusion. Align options do not appear while you edit text inside a text box. Click outside the text, select the box itself, and then try again. The tutorials call this out as a common problem.
Keyboard shortcuts for aligning on Mac

Many search results overstate this part. The only Mac shortcut confirmed for this guide is ⌘G, which groups selected elements. A printable cheat sheet lists no Mac shortcut for aligning, distributing or centering on the page.

Some posts quote Option+Shift+T for Tidy up and Command+Shift with the arrow keys for aligning edges. No source opened for this guide confirmed them, so they are not given here as fact. Test any shortcut on a scratch design first. The cheat sheet warns that shortcuts change with software version, OS and keyboard layout.
Web app or desktop app: what is not known

None of the sources says whether these steps match the Canva web app in a browser. The tutorials also do not say which app version they were recorded in. If you design in a browser, run the align steps there and compare the results before you assume they match.
If you switch between web and desktop, keep one design open in each and check the same option. That check is quick and saves you from a bad export.
Canva version and macOS requirements

The sources disagree on the newest Mac build. FileHorse lists Canva 1.128.0 as the latest Mac version, with a universal build for Intel and Apple silicon. A search snippet gave 1.126.0 instead. The same FileHorse page lists a minimum macOS of 10.13 in one field and 11.0 in another.

Install the current build from a download page you trust, and check that your Mac meets the requirement Canva lists for that build. If your align options look different from the steps here, your build may not match the one the tutorials used. You can check the install steps in [how to download and install Canva on Mac](/how-to/download-and-install-canva-in-canva).
Mistakes people make most often

items: Looking for align options with only one element selected.
Trying to align while the cursor is still inside a text box.
Aligning the parts of a group instead of the group.
Running Tidy up on a layout that was never aligned.
Dragging elements into place and skipping the snap guides.
Trusting a shortcut from a random post without testing it.

blocks.text: Ask Lazur when you cannot find a button
Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold Option and Command, then ask where the Position button is. Lazur sees your screen, draws a circle and a label around it, and answers out loud.

Lazur can also walk you through a whole task. Ask how to do it, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. You still do the clicking. Lazur does not click buttons or edit your design for you.
Next steps after your layout is aligned
Once the layout is clean, you may want to reuse it. [Duplicate a design in Canva on Mac](/how-to/duplicate-a-design-in-canva) shows two ways to copy a finished layout, step by step.

If Canva starts acting strange, [reset the desktop app](/how-to/reset-the-desktop-app-in-canva) explains a reset that keeps your designs. If you lay out work for a specific job, the [Canva for designers page](/for/designers/canva) covers resizing, branding and exporting. To see what Lazur adds inside Canva, read the [Lazur for Canva page](/apps/canva).

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to align elements in Canva on Mac?
faq.answer: Not one that any source confirmed. The only verified Mac shortcut in these sources is ⌘G, which groups selected elements. A cheat sheet lists no Mac shortcut for aligning, so use the Position menu for now.

faq.question: Why don't the align options show up?
faq.answer: Align options need at least two selected elements. Select them by holding Shift and clicking each one. They also disappear while you type inside a text box, so click outside the text first.

faq.question: What is the difference between Center and Middle?
faq.answer: Center lines up elements on their horizontal middle, so they stack on one vertical line. Middle lines up elements on their vertical middle, so they sit on one horizontal line. Pick the one that matches the direction your layout runs.

faq.question: Does Space evenly work with only two elements?
faq.answer: No. Space evenly applies when three or more elements are selected, according to GeniusJunkie. With two elements, use Left, Right, Top or Bottom to line them up instead.

faq.question: Does the Canva web app work the same way?
faq.answer: The sources do not say. Test the align steps in the web app before you rely on them there, and compare the results with the desktop app.

faq.question: Can Lazur align my elements for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. It can circle the Position button, name it, and walk you through each click while you do the clicking.

faq.question: Which macOS version does Canva need?
faq.answer: The sources disagree. FileHorse lists a minimum of 10.13 in one field and 11.0 in another. Check the requirements on the download page for the build you install before you update.

steps.name: Open the design
steps.text: Open your design in the Canva desktop app. Make sure every element you want to align is on the same page.

steps.name: Select the first element
steps.text: Click the first element. A selection outline appears around it.

steps.name: Add the other elements
steps.text: Hold Shift and click each element you want to align. Align options need at least two selected elements.

steps.name: Open Position
steps.text: Look at the top toolbar and click Position. The align options open from here.

steps.name: Pick the edge or center
steps.text: Choose Left, Center, Right, Top, Middle or Bottom. Canva lines the selected elements up on that line.

steps.name: Check the alignment
steps.text: Look at the selection outline and check the edges. Each selected element should share the edge or center you picked.

steps.name: Space evenly for three or more
steps.text: With three or more elements selected, open Position and choose Space evenly. Pick horizontal or vertical spacing to match the layout.

steps.name: Group items that move together
steps.text: If a set of elements should move as one block, select them and press ⌘G to group them. Then align the group.

steps.name: Turn on rulers and grid
steps.text: Open the View menu and choose Show rulers and Show grid. Use them to compare edges with the page.

steps.name: Tidy up uneven gaps
steps.text: If the spacing is still uneven, run Tidy up. Align first, because Tidy up can give odd results on a messy layout.

steps.name: Review the whole page
steps.text: Review the full page after your last change, because a later edit can move elements out of line.

troubleshooting.fix: Select two or more elements. Make sure you are not editing text inside a text box. Click outside the text, then select the elements again.
One tutorial says the Position option may need a click to reveal. That is unverified. Click the element again and look at the top toolbar.

troubleshooting.problem: Tidy up makes the layout worse
troubleshooting.fix: Align the elements first with Position, then run Tidy up. Undo and try again if the result still looks odd.

troubleshooting.problem: Elements look aligned but are slightly off
troubleshooting.fix: Snap guides appear only while you drag. Turn on View > Show rulers and View > Show grid, then compare the edges with the grid lines.

troubleshooting.problem: Space evenly is missing from the menu
troubleshooting.fix: Check that three or more elements are selected. Some tutorials do not list Space evenly, so your build may not show it. Update Canva and check again.
